cells.tense: You are the one who catches what a shared moment is carrying and says it plainly.
cells.ask: Name what you noticed in one conversation today, in plain words, then let it rest.
cells.core:
You catch what's moving between people before it has words, and your version of it lands. In a conversation that's circling, you're the one who says the true thing and the whole thing loosens around it. It isn't performance — the feeling is real, and you hand it back clarified, which is why it moves people. That part is working.

What holds it steady is that you know where your shaping stops and the moment's own life begins. Let the next small picture stand on its own a minute instead of tugging it toward what it could mean for the room. You don't need the whole road visible to take the next step. That's the ground you're on, and you're walking it well.

cells.tense: You're working out what a shared moment will feel like before anyone has entered it.
cells.ask: Take one picture you're carrying for a group and put it in front of someone this week, slowly.
cells.core:
You're already in the next moment. Your mind runs ahead of now, arranging a version of this that will land — before anything has formed. It's been rehearsed so thoroughly it arrives finished, and finished is the one thing it can't be. The arranging has replaced the thing itself, and the push costs you the moment it was for.

Held well, this trusts one step and lets the picture stay half-lit while it takes shape against someone. Show one of them to a person this week, at their pace, and let their half of it change yours. It won't be finished. That's what handing it over is for, and the slow version is the one that holds.

cells.tense: You had something true to say and you are still at the edge of saying it.
cells.ask: Write what you noticed about a recent shared moment, no interpretation, and keep it for yourself.
cells.core:
The moment came and you noticed it and you didn't put it into words. You're parked at the edge of that — near the moment but not inside it, and the catching stopped short of the saying. Nothing is shut. You're just not moving through.

Held well, this takes one step in the half-light and lets the picture show itself as you go, without forcing the whole shape. Don't push yourself back toward the feeling. Work it out instead — think it into plain sense, write the pieces where only you'll read them. That's what brings you current again, and it moves at the speed you can actually walk.

cells.tense: You are already shaping how a moment lands, and you talk as if it shaped itself.
cells.ask: Name one thing you said that shifted a conversation, and say plainly that the words were yours.
cells.core:
It's already happening. You find the one sentence in a mess of them, you take what the room was circling and make it land — and after, you describe it as the moment finding its own way. But it was your words doing it. The hand was on the pen the whole time.

Held well, you can say your part without claiming the room, and the room stays its own life. Pulling the moment back under your name is what keeps it yours instead of anyone's. Name one of those sayings as yours and see how the ground holds. You don't owe anyone the smaller version.
